item: audit recheck P3 P5 P11 P13 P16: restore inflation bound, atomic folder manifest, custody verify names its signer (R681)
key_paths: src/backup/artifact.py; src/backup/folder_backup.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/custody/log.py; src/api/custody.py; tests/test_audit_recheck_lane_b.py
summary: P3: the restore preflight read the archive's size, and a 204 KB zip inflates to 200 MiB; _safe_extract now preflights the sum of the members' declared sizes before writing and copies each member by hand, refusing one that yields more than it declares (zipfile itself already stops at the declared size with a CRC error; this is the second wall); each member and each level of its path is also charged 4 KiB, and member count (200,000) and path depth (64) are capped, because 200 empty members nested 900 levels deep wrote 705 MiB from a 737 KB zip declaring 203 bytes. P5: the signed folder-backup manifest is written through a temp file, fsync and rename. P11/R681: POST /api/custody/verify keeps verified but never alone: signed_by lists each signer with its entry count, and verdict tells verified-against-your-keys from signatures-valid-signer-not-yours (and your-keys-unreadable); yours is said only of a signer whose every signature verified (no probing a key with a junk signature), an empty bundle is not verified, a hybrid half this install does not hold is not yours, a signer key that is not a string reads as not verified rather than a 500, and a verify never creates a key. No UI calls this endpoint, so the wording lives in the API's verdict_text. P13: write_backup_v2's docstring no longer calls it the single-file product path (A-022). P16: restore state files go through a per-write temp name, fsynced, that a failure removes. 18 tests, 17 red on main (the honest-archive one is the non-regression check). Release line: A restore now checks the space a backup will really take once unpacked, so a damaged or crafted backup can no longer fill your data disk; and verifying a custody bundle now says whose keys signed it.
